newsitem.title: USA: Clinton expands law banning sex discrimination.
newsitem.headline: Clinton expands law banning sex discrimination.

text.p: President Bill Clinton Tuesday marked the 25th anniversary of a landmark law that broke down barriers to women in school course offerings, sports and hiring by ordering strengthened enforcement of the statute.

Clinton said Title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972 had had a beneficial effect on every American. "If we've learned anything in the last 25 years since Title IX became law, it is that expanding benefits and opportunities for any American helps the rest of us," he said.

"Every school and every education program that receives federal assistance in the entire country must understand that complying with Title IX is not optional -- it is the law. And the law must be enforced," Clinton said.
He said he was directing every federal department and agency to strengthen its enforcement of the law by reviewing compliance procedures.

Clinton also moved to close a loophole in the law which exempts the military service academies and other government education programs from the requirements of Title IX. White House spokesman Mike McCurry conceded that this action was more symbolic than substantive since most such programs already comply.

Several pioneering women attended the White House ceremony, including astronaut Sally Ride and six-time Olympic gold medalist Jackie Joyner Kersee. "Because of Title IX, I am here," Joyner Kersee said, noting that an athletic scholarship had enabled her to get a college education.
